attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, asserted in his own voice.

semantics.note: The three factual parts are kept. The motive inference is rightly left out. 'Has not found a way' fairly renders 'can't find a way'.

contract.note: The plain reading (no workable monetization, charging under consideration, ongoing hallucinations) is ordinary. Revenue versus profit is left open and the April 2024 window was chosen by the evaluator. Both are flagged fairly.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous report of FT sources saying Google was considering charging for AI search. Supports the charging part only.
Secondary summary of Washington Post testing in which SGE made up details and citations, dated April 1, 2024. Supports the hallucination part.
A 2023 Google post describing ads within SGE. It is a plan from an earlier period and reports no realized revenue or profit.

reviews.rationale: The charging part (e1) and the hallucination part (e2) are supported. The central monetization part is not settled: no SGE revenue, cost or profit figures are in the packet, and the ad plan (e3) shows neither success nor failure. The support condition needs all three parts and no contradiction condition is met, so the claim stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. He relies on a reviewer's findings but states them as his own view.

semantics.note: The proposition makes the quality judgment testable through his specifics: missed requirements, outdated approaches, slower than a human. It is limited to the Upwork demo, which matches the context.

contract.note: Limiting the claim to the demo is fair. The human comparator and the change to the prompt are flagged. The requirements part refers to the client's actual request, which is how the speaker framed it.

evidence.note: Reports the client saying the work was not what he requested. It also lists the reviewer's findings: a crude C-style loop and about 36 minutes for the human versus at least six hours for Devin. This is secondary reporting.
Later reporting that repeats the reviewer's timing comparison of 36 minutes versus six hours. Its separate 2025 evaluation is not relevant here.
Cognition's demonstrator admits the prompt was not the client's verbatim request. This confirms the output did not match the client's request, though it shifts the cause. It is a company statement.

reviews.rationale: Reporting (e1, e2) backs all three specifics: the output did not meet the client's request, the code was crude, and Devin took hours where a human took 36 minutes. Cognition's admission (e3) confirms the output did not match the request, even though the changed prompt explains part of it. The original artifacts were not inspected directly, but the corroborating reports agree and nothing contradicts them.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The universal 'every single' and the hedges are preserved. The hedge 'what appears to be' covers only the rest-of-internet part. The Common Crawl part is unhedged.

contract.note: Reading 'every single' literally is the ordinary reading of firm universal language. The named products are examples, so one documented counterexample is a fair test.

evidence.note: The StarCoder paper limits training to The Stack (GitHub code), with no Common Crawl.
The BigCode repository documents code-generation use and a coding assistant released in May 2023, before the post. This makes StarCoder an application-level counterexample.
LLaMA's mixture does include Common Crawl, so the claim fits one named family. That cannot establish the universal claim.

reviews.rationale: The claim says every LLM-based application is trained on Common Crawl plus other web data. StarCoder and its coding assistant were released before the post and documented as trained only on The Stack's GitHub data (e1, e2). That meets the contract's contradiction condition. The claim does fit some named models, such as LLaMA (e3), but the universal statement fails.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps the general 'AI' scope and both requirements and implementation discussion.

contract.note: Reading 'AI' generally follows his wording. How much competence 'handle' implies is unspecified, which the contract flags. The 2024 window was inferred by the evaluator.

evidence.note: Cognition's own description of Devin collaborating on design choices. A vendor claim with no interaction record attached.
A 2023 study of ChatGPT generating requirements. It predates the window and is narrower than a collaborative discussion.

reviews.rationale: No dated interaction record or independent evaluation from the 2024 window shows AI either succeeding or failing at collaborative discussion of requirements and implementation. The vendor claim (e1) is not enough under the source requirements, and the 2023 study (e2) is out of period and narrower. The packet does not settle the claim.
